Who We Are
Nuro believes self-driving vehicles are the most immediate and profound opportunity for AI to drive positive change in the physical world. Safer streets, more time for what matters, and easier access to the world around us, that’s why we’re building a universal autonomy platform: self-driving for all roads and all rides.
Founded in 2016, Nuro is a physical AI company developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology for a wide range of vehicles, use cases, and markets. Powered by the Nuro Driver™, our universal autonomy platform enables the global mobility ecosystem to deploy autonomy at scale, from robotaxis and logistics fleets to personal vehicles.
With years of real-world deployment experience and a flexible, partner-led business model, Nuro is working toward a future where millions of autonomous vehicles powered by our technology help make everyday life safer, easier, and more connected.
Nuro has raised over $2B in capital from Uber, NVIDIA, Google, Softbank, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, and other leading investors.
About The Role
Nuro operates real self-driving vehicles on public roads today — not a research platform, not ADAS. The Embedded Software Engineering team builds the software for the safety-critical embedded controllers that connect the Nuro Driver™ to the vehicle: the devices that command steering, braking, and propulsion, alongside other vehicle actuators, distribute and monitor power, monitor vehicle motion, and bring the vehicle to a safe state when something goes wrong.
As an Embedded Software Engineer, you will work across the full stack of multicore automotive microcontrollers from RTOS, drivers, and scheduler up through middleware and application components that talk to the vehicle, and help extend that stack as our hardware evolves. You will bring the Nuro Driver™ up on new vehicle platforms alongside OEM and supplier engineers, and see your code drive real vehicles on public roads. We're hiring across levels, from engineers with a couple years of embedded experience to those who've shipped a production automotive launch.
About The Work
Design, implement and test embedded C software for safety-critical multicore automotive microcontrollers, spanning base software such as RTOS, device drivers, scheduling and bootloader, middleware such as inter-component messaging and end-to-end protection, and application components such as actuator interface, body controls, power management and fault management.
Integrate the Nuro Driver™ with new vehicle platforms: define and implement CAN and Ethernet interfaces with OEM ECUs, adapt actuator and body-control interfaces, and validate them on bench and in vehicle.
Take part in hands-on device and vehicle bring-up, prototyping and debugging on multiple vehicle platforms, from first power-on to autonomous driving.
Build and maintain the team's verification infrastructure: unit tests, hardware-in-the-loop benches and vehicle test procedures.
Work within an ISO 26262 development process: define software requirements from system safety requirements, then implement and verify them with full traceability.
Collaborate daily with systems, safety, hardware, controls and autonomy engineers, and with OEM and supplier partners, from definition through verification.
About You
B.S. or higher in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a closely related field.
2+ years of industry experience developing embedded software in C, including work on a real-time operating system.
Solid computer science fundamentals: data structures, concurrency and algorithm design.
Working knowledge of microcontroller internals and peripherals, with depth in at least one of device driver development, CAN or automotive Ethernet, bootloaders and software update, embedded security, or vehicle-level integration and test.
Strong problem-solving and debugging skills, clear written and spoken communication, and a track record of working well with engineers from other disciplines.
Comfortable at the bench with debug probes, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers and CAN tools. You enjoy finding out why hardware and software disagree.
Bonus Points
3+ years of embedded development in the automotive or autonomous vehicle industry, including a production launch.
Hands-on functional safety experience with ISO 26262, or safety-critical development in another regulated industry such as DO-178C or IEC 62304.
Experience with Infineon AURIX TC3xx, SafeRTOS or FreeRTOS, or AUTOSAR Classic base software such as MCAL and communication stacks.
Vehicle network integration experience: DBC and ARXML, UDS diagnostics, E2E protection, time synchronization.
Knowledge of vehicle functions, vehicle dynamics or control theory.
At Nuro, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. For this position, the reasonably expected base pay range is between $145,830 and $219,000 for the level at which this job has been scoped. Your base pay will depend on several factors, including your experience, qualifications, education, location, and skills. In the event that you are considered for a different level, a higher or lower pay range would apply. Amazon Leo (formerly Project Kuiper) is an initiative to launch a constellation of Low Earth Orbit satellites that will provide low-latency, high-speed broadband network connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world.
Have you wanted an opportunity to secure an advanced satellite based broadband telecom service? The Amazon Leo Security team owns the security of product and operations of Amazon Leo end-to-end. We provide the necessary infrastructure and mechanisms to ensure the security of our satellite constellation and to protect the integrity and confidentiality of our customer data. Our team drives the research & development, deployment and operation of several mission-critical security systems and mechanisms. You will work in a start-up like environment, backed by Amazon’s infrastructure to bootstrap security mechanisms, and help instill the security culture in the organization.
Export Control Requirement - Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen.
Key job responsibilities
You will be responsible for working with security engineers on the team and builders in Leo to develop security tooling for automating the security review process, identifying security issues in existing product code-bases and cloud infrastructure, and helping our team move at machine speed.
You will collaborate with builder teams to assess technical debt and risk. You will provide strategic direction that addresses vulnerabilities and fortifies our products. You will be a resource that leads the burn down of long-term risk.
You will guide teams towards solutions that are secure by default. If secure-by-default solutions don’t exist, you will invent & propose them. You will leverage support from automation teams that find discoverable vulnerabilities. You will advocate for the creation & deployment of new testing tools, and detection mechanisms.
You will enable builder teams to become proactive & self-sufficient on security. You will work with builder teams to understand their build processes. You'll ensure that they use appropriate security linting & static analysis tools. You'll help our builders find security solutions that reduce security operations costs over time. You will instill a security culture in builder teams. You will mentor builders who aspire to become security advocates & security engineers via 1-1 sessions & office hours.
You will propose a security vision for the business that delivers security that protects our customers.
And last of all, you will hack some really cool bleeding edge tech!

In this highly dynamic role, you'll be accountable for deciding where your time investments provide the most value. You will have a blend of proactive and reactive work. Teams will reach out for ideas on how to handle a wide variety of security problems. You can anticipate implementation questions like
"What's the right way to handle authentication tokens in service to service communications?"
"We need to define security requirements for a confidential new product launch."
"We've experienced an incident and need to perform 5 why's analysis to identify and correct the problem that produced the incident."

Diverse Experiences
Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. Why Amazon Security?
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build
experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.
Inclusive Team Culture
In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.
Training & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.
Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Unlock the Future of Space at Redwire Space
Do you thrive on turning the impossible into reality? At Redwire Space, every day presents an opportunity to innovate, tackle fascinating challenges, and directly shape future technologies for multiple domains (space and terrestrial). Redwire is where groundbreaking ideas take flight, and the results are truly out of this world.
Innovate with Our RF Systems Group in Longmont, Colorado
Join Redwire's RF Systems group in Longmont, Colorado, and become an integral part of engineering the next generation of RF products. These enable mission-critical capabilities across space, air, land, and beyond. Whether it's advanced communications, sophisticated sensing, electronic warfare, or directed energy, our team delivers cutting-edge solutions — from orbital deployments to the tactical edge — in support of
one force, every front
.
Join a Team Driven by Curiosity, Purpose, and Impact
Decide today to become a part of our engineering team and you'll find yourself in a collaborative, agile environment where curiosity, purpose, and impact guide every decision. We are not just a company; we are a collective renowned for our technical expertise, leadership in engineering, and unwavering commitment to project ownership. Come experience a place where your contributions truly matter.
Redwire Space Solutions has an opportunity for an
RF Engineer I at our facility in Longmont, CO
. This is an early-career role for an engineer who wants to build a strong foundation in RF systems engineering through modeling, simulation, and analysis. Working alongside senior RF engineers, you will develop and correlate simulation models of RF components and systems, build the software tools that make our analysis faster and more repeatable, and follow those designs through build, test, and delivery. We are building RF systems for new space and multiple domain communications architectures. This requisition is aimed at candidates completing a bachelor's degree in December 2026, with an anticipated start date in January 2027.
Responsibilities
Develop, correlate, and maintain RF simulation models of components, subassemblies, and end-to-end systems using industry standard tools such as Keysight ADS, in order to predict performance and evaluate design trades ahead of hardware build.
Perform RF component data sheet review and trade studies to compare candidate devices and optimize RF system architecture and performance against gain, noise, linearity, power, size, and cost objectives.
Build three-dimensional electromagnetic models of RF devices and assemblies in Ansys HFSS, including cavity and enclosure analysis of active devices, to characterize resonances, coupling, and packaging effects that drive gain, isolation, and stability.
Perform schematic capture and layout of RF printed circuit boards, applying high-frequency design practices such as controlled-impedance transmission lines, grounding and return-path management, and isolation between stages.
Develop and maintain scripts and software utilities that automate simulation setup, measurement data reduction, and report generation, improving the throughput and repeatability of the RF team's day-to-day analysis work.
Apply engineering principles to ensure designed components and systems meet all requirements such as operational frequency range, signal to noise ratio, system linearity, and stability.
Support the development, qualification, and delivery of high-performance RF systems for space and multi domain environments, under the guidance and mentorship of senior RF engineers.
Support RF characterization and verification activities in the laboratory and during flight build, test, and delivery. Assist with test setup, collect and process measurement data to verify specifications, and correlate measured results back to simulation models.
Interface with multi-disciplinary team members to optimize component and system designs that meet all technical, cost and schedule requirements.
Support the development, management, and maintenance of system designs and their associated documentation - CAD, Drawings, BOMs, analysis reports, and test procedures.
Contribute simulation results, analysis products, and supporting data to project stage-gate reviews (such as PDR, CDR).
Ideal Experience
B.S. in Electrical Engineering, Engineering with an electrical specialty, Applied Mathematics, or Physics, with coursework, undergraduate research, or project focus in RF design and analysis. Candidates completing their degree in December 2026 are encouraged to apply.
0-2 years of professional experience. Internship, co-op, undergraduate research, or teaching and laboratory assistant experience in RF, electronics, or hardware development is considered in lieu of full-time industry experience.
Hands-on knowledge of RF simulation techniques and software, including circuit- and system-level simulation of RF components and signal chains and/or three-dimensional electromagnetic modeling of RF structures.
Working knowledge of RF fundamentals, including S-parameters, impedance matching, transmission lines, gain and noise figure cascading, linearity, and stability.
Proficiency with at least one scripting or programming language, such as Python, MATLAB, or C++, and a demonstrated interest in applying software to automate engineering analysis, data processing, and repetitive design tasks.
Familiarity with schematic capture and printed circuit board layout tools, such as Altium Designer, Cadence, OrCAD, or KiCad.
Familiarity with standard RF characterization tests and test equipment such as vector network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, signal generators and power meters, gained through coursework, laboratory, or internship experience.

About Mass Culture
Mass Culture is a growth media agency. We help mission-driven scale-ups connect brand and performance so they grow faster, more profitably, and with purpose.
About The Role
Mass Culture is a paid media agency and growth partner for mission-driven scale-up brands. We build and run our own client portal: the product our clients log into to see their media plans, budget pacing, cross-channel performance, and the reports we deliver.
We're looking for a part-time engineer to build features in it end to end, and to make them look as good as they work.
What You'll Build
Client-facing surfaces: dashboards, widgets, charts, and the report and deck builders. This is what clients see and react to, and it carries the agency's credibility.
Admin surfaces: the widget builder, plan editor, pacing tools, and configuration panels our team uses every day.
The data plumbing a feature needs: Postgres schema and migrations, server actions, and connector work against ad-platform APIs.
Polish passes on surfaces that already work but don't yet feel finished.
The Stack
Layer
What We Use
Framework
Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript
Data
Supabase — Postgres, Auth, row-level security, BigQuery
Styling
Tailwind CSS v4, Radix UI, a token-based design system
Charts
visx
Editors & interaction
Tiptap, dnd-kit, Zustand
Tooling
bun, Vercel
What We Mean By a Good Eye
You can take a rough spec and produce a surface that looks considered, without being handed a mockup.
You work in the design system rather than around it. Components reference semantic color tokens only, never a raw palette value and never a bare rgba literal, and every dark-mode token has a light-mode counterpart. When the system is missing something, you extend the system.
You notice spacing, alignment, and type hierarchy without being asked, and you care about the difference between 12px and 16px.
You can make a chart readable, not just correct. Charts are where most of our design problems live.
You know the difference between a surface that is done and one that is merely working.
How We Work Together
Asynchronous and autonomous. You pick up scoped work, build it in a branch, and open a pull request. We review and merge. Nothing merges itself.
We write things down. Specs, design docs, and house conventions live in the repo. Read them before you fight them.
Verify your own work. A green test suite is not the bar. We have shipped bugs with a fully green suite, which is why we now expect you to open the page, look at it, and say what you saw.
This codebase is built heavily with AI coding tools. You are welcome to use them and expected to review what they produce as carefully as you would review your own work. Judgment is the job. Typing isn't.
Say when something is wrong, including when we are wrong about it.
Required
What We're Looking For:
Strong React and TypeScript, with real Next.js App Router experience: server components, server actions, and caching behavior.
Comfort with SQL and relational data modeling. You can write a migration and reason about what a query is actually doing.
Work you designed as well as built, in a portfolio or a repo we can look at. A few well-made things beat a long list.
The ability to work independently in an unfamiliar, opinionated codebase and match its conventions rather than impose your own.
Clear written communication. Most of our collaboration is text.
Reliable part-time availability. Consistency matters more than volume.
Nice To Have
Data visualization experience, especially charts built on real, messy data.
Supabase or Postgres row-level security experience.
Experience with analytics, reporting, or BI-style products.
Comfort in design tools, though we will not ask you to produce mockups.
Engagement
Part-time, freelance, remote, and ongoing. Hours and rate are flexible and agreed up front. We start with a small paid scoped project so both sides can find out whether it's a fit before committing to more.
To apply, send a note and a link to something you designed and built.

As part of Intersect’s Microgrid Engineering team, you’ll define and implement the validation framework that ensures microgrid control software performs safely and reliably before deployment. This team plays a critical role in advancing Intersect’s mission to accelerate the clean energy transition, designing and operating systems that deliver reliable power at massive scale. The Microgrid Engineering team works across software, hardware, operations, and external stakeholders to validate complex systems under realistic conditions, ensuring safety, performance, and long-term operability. Create scalable validation processes that support the continued growth and deployment of microgrid systems.
Define Test Cases and Performance Criteria

Verify controller behavior under both normal operating conditions and abnormal system events.
Establish objective performance metrics and acceptance criteria to evaluate system readiness.
Integrate Field Learnings into Validation
Analyze field operating data to improve simulation fidelity and identify previously untested edge cases.
Incorporate operational insights into regression test suites to continuously strengthen validation coverage.
Support root-cause investigations and validation efforts for system performance issues.
Maintain Validation Assets and Traceability
Expand and maintain laboratory validation capabilities, including HIL environments and supporting test infrastructure.
Troubleshoot issues related to test equipment, simulation platforms, and validation workflows.

B.S. or M.S. in Electrical Engineering, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
2-5+ years of experience in real-time system HIL validation, SIL testing, power system model verification, or related validation disciplines.

Hands-on experience with real-time simulators and validation platforms, including SIL, HIL, or comparable testing environments.
Familiarity with simulation and modeling tools such as Simulink, Modelica, or similar platforms.
Experience supporting commissioning, troubleshooting, or operational validation of laboratory or utility-scale power systems.

Experience using modern software development practices, including version control, automated testing, and validation workflows.

https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/44694.description_preview:
Own how fast, how cheaply and how reliably models run on our infrastructure. Throughput, latency and cost per unit of work, from the serving layer down to the kernel.
‍
About Orbifold AI
Orbifold AI is building the infrastructure layer for Physical AI. As intelligent systems move beyond language into the physical world, they require a fundamentally new understanding of physics, action, and interaction.
We partner with leading robotics and world model research teams to advance the foundations of embodied intelligence, enabling intelligent systems to perceive, understand, and operate in the real world.
The standards we set, and the infrastructure we build to scale them, will define the next frontier of robotics and Physical AI.
‍
Role Overview
Everything we deliver is produced by a model running on our infrastructure. Perception models, evaluation models, verification models, and increasingly our partners’ own models. The inputs are video and sensor data rather than short text, the volume grows every month, and the economics of the entire platform run through how efficiently that work executes.
You own that execution layer. Serving architecture on Ray and PyTorch, batching and scheduling, memory fit, quantization, compiler and kernel level work where it pays, and the profiling discipline that tells you which of those is actually the bottleneck today rather than which one is the most interesting.
This is a performance role with a direct product consequence. Every improvement you land buys more thorough evaluation, more verification passes, and more partner workloads on the same hardware. It is also a founding seat: the inference function at Orbifold is what you decide it is.
‍
What You Will Work On
Own model serving end to end. Design and run the serving layer for our production models on Ray Serve and PyTorch, across a heterogeneous GPU fleet with very uneven workload shapes.
Drive throughput and utilization. Batching strategies, scheduling, concurrency, queueing, and the unglamorous work of finding out why a GPU is sitting at forty percent.
Make models fit. Quantization, precision selection, memory layout, activation and cache management, together with the measurement that proves output quality did not move when you did.
Go down a level when it pays. Compiler paths, operator fusion, custom CUDA or Triton kernels where the off-the-shelf version is leaving real performance on the table, and the judgment to know when it is not.
Serve the awkward workloads. High-volume video and multimodal inference, evaluation harnesses, and reinforcement learning environments that need many fast rollouts rather than one large request.
Build the benchmarking harness that makes performance claims reproducible instead of anecdotal, and keeps regressions from shipping quietly.
Run it in production. Autoscaling, fault tolerance, graceful degradation, observability, and cost per workload that anyone in the company can look up.
Bring partner models onto our infrastructure: packaging, throughput and memory fit, validation that what we return matches what they get locally, and an honest account of where it does not.
‍
What We Are Looking For
3+ years building production machine learning systems, with deep Python and PyTorch.
You have owned inference performance for a real workload, and you can describe the profile before and after in numbers rather than adjectives.
A working mental model of GPU execution: memory hierarchy and bandwidth, kernel launch overhead, occupancy, and where the time actually goes.
Experience operating a distributed serving or compute framework such as Ray or Kubernetes under real production load.
Comfortable being measured on throughput, latency and cost, including the weeks when the number does not move.
Judgment about when to optimize and when to leave something alone. Most of the value is in choosing correctly.
‍
Nice to Have
CUDA, Triton, or compiler level work (torch.compile, TensorRT, XLA, or similar).
Video or multimodal inference at scale: hardware decode, preprocessing, batching across variable-length inputs.
Quantization, distillation or speculative methods taken all the way into production.
Ray Serve, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, or comparable serving stacks.
Serving diffusion, video generation, or vision language action models.
Open-source contributions to a serving or performance stack that other engineers rely on.
Why This Role
Performance is the business. Compute is the dominant cost of what we do, so the work you own is visible at the level of what the company can afford to attempt.
The playbook is not written. Serving video and embodied models behaves almost nothing like serving text, and very few people have solved it at scale yet.
Full vertical ownership, from the serving API down to the kernel, without an abstraction layer separating you from the hardware.
Frontier workloads and real hardware, at a size where a single good decision is measurable within a week.
‍
How To Apply
Please send your resume and any relevant work, papers, projects, repos, to
careers@orbifold.ai
.

Build the product surface of our platform: the console partners run workloads from, the viewer they inspect results in, and the SDK that puts both in their own code.
‍
About Orbifold AI
Orbifold AI is building the infrastructure layer for Physical AI. As intelligent systems move beyond language into the physical world, they require a fundamentally new understanding of physics, action, and interaction.
We partner with leading robotics and world model research teams to advance the foundations of embodied intelligence, enabling intelligent systems to perceive, understand, and operate in the real world.
The standards we set, and the infrastructure we build to scale them, will define the next frontier of robotics and Physical AI.
‍
Role Overview
The infrastructure underneath is good and almost entirely invisible. Partners reach it today largely through us, through conversations, handoffs and engineers on both sides. That is how every infrastructure company starts, and it is not how any of them scale.
You will build what the partner touches. The console where a research team submits workloads and watches them run. The viewer where they inspect a result properly rather than taking our word for it. The SDK and API that let them do all of it from inside their own pipeline, without talking to anyone. This is the difference between a service and a platform, and right now it is one seat.
It is a genuinely full-stack role: media-heavy interfaces in the browser, real services behind them, and API contracts that outside engineers will depend on. Your users are research engineers at some of the most demanding labs in the world, which is a high bar and very fast feedback.
‍
What You Will Work On
Build the partner console: submit and monitor workloads, see status, throughput and progress, and understand what is happening without asking us.
Build the multi-stream and 3D viewer. Synchronized playback across views, overlays on reconstructed output, frame-accurate inspection, in the browser, at real data sizes.
Design and own the SDK and public API. Clean, versioned, documented, and adoptable by a research engineer in an afternoon. This is the surface our reputation as a platform will rest on.
Build the internal tooling our own operators and researchers use, on the same foundations, the same primitives should serve both.
Own the vertical end to end: TypeScript front end, Python services behind it, and the contracts in between.
Work directly with partners on what they actually need, rather than through a layer of translation.
‍
What We Are Looking For
4+ years shipping production web applications, with strong modern TypeScript and real front-end engineering depth.
You have built media-heavy or data-heavy interfaces, video, 3D, or large datasets rendered in a browser, and you know why the naive approach stops working.
Demonstrated API or SDK design for external consumers, and opinions about what makes one pleasant to adopt.
Comfortable across the stack into Python services and infrastructure, rather than stopping at the API boundary.
Product instinct. You will often be the person who notices the workflow is wrong, not just the code.
Self-driven and high agency, with experience in fast-paced applied research or startup environments.
‍
Nice to Have
WebGL, Three.js, WebCodecs, or equivalent, rendering and decoding at scale in the browser.
Video or 3D tooling: players, annotation interfaces, timeline editors, point-cloud or mesh viewers.
A developer-facing SDK you shipped that external engineers actually adopted.
ML tooling, labeling, or experiment platforms.
Familiarity with distributed compute (Ray, Kubernetes) and what it is like to build a UI over something that is genuinely distributed.
Design sensibility, and the willingness to use it.
Why This Role
You build the first product surface this company has had. Almost nothing is decided yet, including the shape of it.
Your users are research engineers at frontier labs: demanding, specific, and quick to tell you when something is wrong.
Turn a service into a platform. That transition is the single highest-leverage thing an engineer can do at our stage, and this is the seat that does it.
Real range: 3D rendering, distributed systems, developer experience, rather than one screen for two years.
‍
How To Apply
Please send your resume and any relevant work, papers, projects, repos, to
careers@orbifold.ai
.

Are you someone who wants hands-on experience building the tooling and knowledge infrastructure behind an agentic software development lifecycle? Are you ready to take the next step in your career by building integrations and knowledge bases that other engineering teams will depend on every day? Are you ready to work alongside experienced engineers on a small, high-visibility platform team? If the answer to all of the above questions is "Yes," come join the world's leading professional services firm. If you are prepared and poised to take the next step in your career, you can help build the platform that powers agentic software delivery across a global business. Then we want to talk to you.
Work you'll do
As a Senior Consultant, Agentic Engineering Platform, you will work alongside the team's Manager and other engineers to build the infrastructure that underpins our agentic software development lifecycle. Day to day, you will write Python to build APIs, automate workflows, and clean and structure the data (both structured and unstructured) that feeds our knowledge bases and tooling. You will build retrieval-augmented generation pipelines against vector databases, using embeddings and evaluation techniques to keep the LLM Wiki and AWS Bedrock-managed knowledge bases accurate and grounded. Beyond these integrations, you will build tools, utilities, and workflows, drawing on pandas, NumPy, and SQL, that help technical program managers identify risk and cross-project dependencies by processing information across the platforms our programs already use. Build data and knowledge foundations that prepare structured and unstructured information for the LLM Wiki and AWS Bedrock-managed knowledge bases.
Engineer grounded AI capabilities by developing retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, agentic workflows, evaluation harnesses, and guardrails that improve accuracy, reliability, and safety.
Connect the agentic software development lifecycle by integrating AWS Kiro, Azure DevOps, ServiceNow, and related platforms to automate the flow of program artifacts, defects, pull requests, and code updates.
Develop production-ready platform capabilities including backend services, APIs, lightweight user interfaces, deployment pipelines, logging, and monitoring that enable teams to use tools without direct API access.
Deliver iterative, well-documented solutions that improve visibility into program risks and dependencies, reduce manual effort, and help engineering and technical program management teams adopt and extend the platform.
A successful candidate would possess these skills:
Communicates clearly and confidently with technical and non-technical audiences, translating complex ideas, trade-offs, and priorities into simple language.
Collaborates effectively across teams by building trust, aligning stakeholders, and moving work forward in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment.
Shows initiative and sound judgment by staying organized, adapting quickly to changing needs, and delivering high-quality work with minimal direction.
The team
At Deloitte Tax LLP, our Global Employer Services (GES) Technology Group consultants help multinational clients develop programs, processes and digital offerings to manage a global workforce and the compliance obligations arising from global mobility, business travel and remote working. People within our technology group come from a diverse background - they partner with our go-to-market teams and global clients to solve challenging problems and design experiences and products that anticipate what our Deloitte clients will want and solutions that keep them compliant with global and local regulations.
Qualifications
Required:
Ability to perform job responsibilities within a hybrid work model that requires US Tax professionals to co-locate in person 2 - 3 days per week
Bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, engineering, or a related field.
3+ years of hands-on Python experience, including building APIs, writing automated tests, debugging, and scripting for automation.
Experience with SQL and data preprocessing, including data cleaning, feature handling, and working with both structured and unstructured data.
Working knowledge of core data science libraries such as pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn, with basic exposure to visualization libraries such as Matplotlib or Seaborn for analysis and evaluation.
Solid understanding of LLM and generative AI fundamentals, including prompting, embeddings, retrieval-augmented generation, vector databases, evaluation methods, guardrails, and hallucination management.
Experience building chains, tools, or agents with LangChain, LangGraph, or a comparable orchestration framework for stateful AI workflows.
Experience using AWS services programmatically via Boto3, including S3, Lambda, Bedrock, DynamoDB, and Agent Core, to support deployment workflows.
Experience with API integrations across at least two enterprise platforms (for example, Azure DevOps, ServiceNow, Jira, Confluence).
Experience with backend deployment practices, including FastAPI, Docker, CI/CD, logging, and monitoring.

About Fractio
Professional services firms now deliver client work with two inputs: human judgment and AI. Their billing, cost, and project management systems were built for a one-input world where every hour is a human hour. So they can't see what AI actually cost to produce a deliverable, or what the human judgment behind it was worth.

Firms see their true cost of producing expertise for every deliverable, then roll it up across clients, teams, practice areas, and their entire book of business. With that view, they decide whether to keep, share, scale, or expand the margin AI creates.

• Workflow integrations: Help connect delivery work in the tools firms already use (Jira, Asana, Linear, Notion, Monday) to Fractio, where outcomes are verified and settled.
• Anomaly detection: Prototype detection for unusual patterns that distort cost data across many deliverables.

About Us
LexReg is a regulatory intelligence platform for banks, credit unions, and fintechs. We offer the LexRegPulse and LexRegulator platforms. LexRegPulse monitors more than 130 federal and state regulatory and industry sources overnight and publishes a synthesized intelligence brief by 6:45 AM ET. Underneath the brief sits the thing that actually matters: a structured, versioned corpus of U.S. banking regulation, broken down into individual, separately citable obligations — the corpus that powers LexRegulator, our charter-scoped AI compliance agent.
Our product promise is that every claim we make traces to a real obligation, every obligation traces to a pinned primary source, and every source is being watched for change. Nothing is paraphrased. Nothing is asserted without a citation a customer can click. Only signal, no noise. This is the bleeding edge of legal and compliance utilization of Agentic AI and the future of the practice.
That promise is only as good as the systems that enforce it.
The Role
You will work with our team and help build products, end to end, across three areas:
Partner platforms
. Products that other companies’ engineers integrate against. You take these from a conversation with the business to production.
The corpus and the checks around it
. Collectors for sources that publish a PDF with no stable URL and no change notification. The schema and its versioning: supersession, amendments, effective dates, and applicability by charter type and asset threshold.
The tooling and the alarms
. The review console, and the per-source health, extraction-yield, and alerts.
How We Work
Agents propose, humans dispose. Automation drafts; it never commits. The commit moment is always a human click. Your job is to make that click well-informed, fast, and reversible —never to route around it.
Work arrives in a queue with a recommendation attached. If we are relying on anyone to remember to check something, we have built it wrong.
Fail loud, never fail quiet. Silent degradation is the only unacceptable outcome.
Deterministic beats probabilistic. If a check can be a string comparison, a schema constraint, or an HTTP status code, it is not an LLM judgment.
The same standard applies to our own code. We have shipped a quality bar no score could reach, and a verdict computed from a field that was never loaded. Both passed review. Finding that class of defect is the job, not an interruption to it.
Who You Are
We hire for the bar, not the résumé.
A current undergraduate or graduate student in engineering, computer science or a related field, or a recent graduate, able to commit 25–35 hours per week.
Working TypeScript and SQL, and a real project you can show — shipped, public, or from an internship or research — that ingests or parses data from a source that did not cooperate.
Or
Two or more years building data-intensive systems in production and keeping them honest. Fluent in TypeScript and SQL; comfortable in Postgres and Prisma. You have designed a schema you later had to migrate, and you have opinions about it now.
You have parsed hostile inputs: inconsistent HTML, PDFs with no text layer, tables that are images, and pagination that changes shape.
You have shipped something that works with an LLM, and you are appropriately skeptical of it. You have been burned by a model that was fluent and wrong; you built a check instead of a better prompt.
Required
Familiarity with AI platforms and using AI to enable efficient development.
You work alongside agentic coding tools and treat their output as a draft written in a confident voice. You can tell a plausible difference from a correct one. When the build is green, your instinct is to verify the claim against production rather than merge.
No ego about escalating.
Intellectual curiosity and honesty under commercial pressure. You will sometimes be the person saying a pipeline is not good enough to ship.
Helpful, Not Required
Bank or credit union compliance, examination, or supervisory correspondence.

This is a deeply hands-on role for an engineer who lives at the seam between hardware and software: you’ll be the person in the lab with a display panel in one hand and a terminal in the other — wiring cameras and screens, standing up compute nodes, writing and debugging the orchestration code that drives them, and chasing a single dropped frame from the GPU decoder all the way to the glass. You will take SNV from the Class B engineering bench, through the cabin-representative Class A mockup, toward flight-worthy production hardware — owning integration, bring-up, and verification at every step. If you want your fingerprints on a system passengers will remember for the rest of their lives, this is it.

Diagnose the hard, cross-domain problems — a wall that won’t span, a node that won’t hold a camera view, a decode stall on a 27 GB asset, a Mac that drops off the managed switch — and drive each to root cause.
Partner across teams and vendors — camera, display, compute, and CMS/avionics groups, plus external build/fab partners (such as the Roush cabin mockup) — to align interfaces and hit integration milestones.
Help mature the system toward certification — supporting DO-178C / DO-254 / DO-160G artifacts and DAL-D discipline as SNV transitions from lab to flight hardware.

Build an understanding of the Cerebras architecture, instruction set, memory system, and communication model.

Build and operate hybrid indexing technology at scale across large clusters, spanning keyword-based sparse-vector indices, embedding-based semantic indices, and emerging semantic-ID indexing driven by next-token prediction. Own the full index lifecycle, and expose clean, unified contracts to the search primitives and recipes that agents compose on top of the corpus.
Design and run high-throughput ingestion and enrichment pipelines that produce a multi-representation, permission-aware corpus at index time. Orchestrate the stages that make content agent-ready, including parsing, chunking, embedding, entity resolution, and access control, and evolve them as new agentic use cases emerge.
Build and operate multi-modal indexing across the full mix of enterprise data, from free text and structured content such as tables to diagrams, images, and audio and video. Represent each modality so it is retrievable through a unified surface, letting agents find the right material regardless of its form or source.
Contribute to a knowledge graph that resolves entities across enterprise data sources, letting agents link disparate resources such as tickets, files, and people through canonical entity relationships.
Improve the performance, scalability, and observability of search, including query latency, indexing throughput, and cluster health, to deliver low-latency, high-quality agentic search experiences. Apply techniques such as vector quantization to balance model quality, retrieval performance, and storage cost.
Own search infrastructure end to end, from intake and design through rollout and ongoing operations, and help shape the search roadmap as the platform grows to support new agents, primitives, and recipes, including needs not yet anticipated.
Drive reliability and operability across the platform through index lifecycle policies, capacity planning, and cluster scaling strategies that keep a growing library of reusable search capabilities healthy in production.
This is a highly collaborative, in-person role, working cross-functionally with Search Ranking, ML, and Platform engineering teams to deliver robust, production-grade agentic search capabilities.

1+ years of full-time industry experience.
Hands-on experience with search technologies; proficiency in one or more search technologies such as Lucene, Solr, Elasticsearch, or OpenSearch is required, with additional experience in vector databases being an advantage.
Excited to be part of an in-person team culture, collaborating on-site with colleagues every day.

About Assembled
Assembled helps companies scale great customer support. As consumers, we’ve all been there. You need help, you’re stuck on hold or going in circles with an AI, and your problem still isn’t solved.
Behind great support is a complex operational problem: thousands of people and AI agents working across teams, time zones, and products as new problems emerge. Assembled gives support leaders the tools to manage that complexity, from AI agents that resolve customer issues to software that forecasts demand, builds schedules, and makes intraday adjustments.
More than 400 companies, including DoorDash, Salesforce, Stripe, and Sephora, trust Assembled. We've raised $71M from NEA, Emergence Capital, Stripe, and Basis Set Ventures and have offices in San Francisco, New York, and London.
About The Role
The Workforce Operations team is building AI agents to automate one of the most operationally complex parts of workforce management: running support in real time. Today, workforce analysts spend their days monitoring live support volume, staffing, and performance, then making constant adjustments to keep coverage on track and response times fast. We believe AI agents can assist with, and eventually autonomously make, many of these decisions—fundamentally changing how teams run their support operations.
This is a 0→1 product area built on top of Assembled’s core workforce management platform. You’ll get the ownership and ambiguity of building something new, while working within a mature product with significant scale, existing complexity, and real customer workflows. It’s an opportunity to figure out what an AI-native approach to workforce operations looks like—and build it for the real world from day one.
This is an onsite role based in our San Francisco office, five days a week (Monday–Friday).
What You'll Work On
You'll own problems end-to-end: from understanding how workforce teams make decisions today, through the data models and systems that power those decisions, to polished product experiences that customers rely on every day. Representative projects from this team:
Building an AI agent for real-time workforce management that monitors support volume, staffing, and performance, identifies emerging problems, and recommends or takes action.
Giving the agent the context and tools it needs to make good decisions, combining live operational data, historical patterns, customer-specific policies, and the capabilities of Assembled’s WFM platform.
Designing the control and observability layer for autonomous operations, so workforce teams can understand what the agent sees, why it recommends an action, and when they want it to act automatically.
Evolving our core Workforce Operations product to support increasingly real-time and automated workflows at the scale and reliability our customers expect.
You might be a great fit if you
Have 2+ years of experience building software products.
Have shipped products end-to-end. You can point to something you helped take from idea to production, explain the product and technical tradeoffs you made, and tell us how customers responded.
Are a strong generalist. You move across the stack without ceremony and pick up new domains quickly. You care more about solving the problem than which layer it lives in.
Like turning ambiguity into working software. You've taken something where the product, technical architecture, or right abstraction wasn't obvious and driven it to a real outcome.
Care about how systems behave in the real world. You think about reliability, edge cases, noisy data, and what happens when software is making decisions that affect a live operation.
Have strong product judgment. You don't just implement requirements; you ask what the user is trying to accomplish and help figure out the right solution.
Sweat the details. You've caught yourself fixing a misaligned pixel or rewriting an error message nobody asked you to, because shipping something sloppy bothers you.
Nice To Have (but Truly Not Required)
Experience building AI agents or AI-powered products. You’ve thought about evaluation, observability, tool use, guardrails, or earning user trust in autonomous systems.
Experience with real-time or data-intensive products. You’ve built systems where fresh data, reliability, and making sense of many changing signals matter.
We know great candidates don’t always meet every requirement listed in a job description. If the role excites you and you believe you can make an impact at Assembled, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and are committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels like they belong and has the opportunity to do their best work. We look forward to hearing from you!

Attackers increasingly operate at agent speed, so we’re building defenses that can keep pace.
Security at Harvey is an engineering discipline, not a gatekeeper function. We build platforms and libraries that make it hard for engineers to get security wrong, and we measure ourselves on adoption and outcomes rather than tickets filed. Create secure-by-default libraries, paved-road abstractions, self-service tooling, and agentic workflows that automate security triage, remediation, and evidence collection
Take security systems from design through production, accounting for trust boundaries, attacker paths, and operational failure modes while owning their reliability and security

Qumulo is a software-defined cloud data platform. Our core is a distributed storage operating system in C & Rust, holding exabytes in the datacenter, at the edge, and natively in the cloud. Qumulo serves everything from a hospital's medical imaging archive to an animation studio's render farm in an environment where 99% correct doesn’t cut it.
About the Role:
Joining us, you'd learn and work across our distributed storage engine and the services that help customers store, manage, and protect their data, under the guidance of experienced senior engineers.
This includes a fault-tolerant block layer that erasure-codes and distributes data beneath the file system, a transactional file system where aggregates roll up as they change so a query across billions of files answers in real time instead of walking a tree, and that same machinery drives quotas, capacity trends, snapshot policy, multiple access protocols, plus replication and backup - all running in userspace.
All of which makes Qumulo a distributed operating system problem: scheduling, memory hierarchy, protection, and concurrency. We're AI-forward and specific about what that means. You will learn to use agents to help write code while developing your engineering judgment to ensure every design decision is correct, because nothing ships that isn't right.
Why join Qumulo:
Qumulo blends the flexibility of a startup with the security of a mature and profitable organization. Here you’ll work closely with a small team of smart, capable engineers who will serve as your mentors. Opinions are expected, disagreement is normal, and you'll get hands-on experience taking projects from ideation to release. We value quality, correctness, and performance. Our architecture, protocols, and patents are public, so you can read how most of this works before you talk to us - and we’re small enough that the work you do will actually show up in the product.
As a Software Engineer at Qumulo, you will:
Collaborate with team members on design, code reviews, and pair programming to deliver high-quality software.
Collaborate with team members and area leads on architecture and design of new/updated features.
Contribute to full-lifecycle feature development and testing using C, Rust, and Python.
Take ownership of defining and implementing customer-facing features and internal system improvements.
Help debug, troubleshoot, and fix test failures and complex product or service issues in production environments.
What we're looking for:
Recently graduated (or graduating within the next 9 months) with a degree in Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent experience.
Ability to write well-factored, maintainable, and well-tested code.
Strong grasp of algorithms and data structures, with solid academic or project experience in distributed systems, database concepts, concurrent programming, or operating systems concepts.
Proficiency in C, C++, Rust, Java, or Go demonstrated through classes, internships, or personal projects
Willingness to work collaboratively with a team to solve complex problems and learn quickly on the job.
Ability to work a hybrid schedule from our downtown Seattle HQ
Must be authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship or transfer. This role is hybrid, based at our downtown Seattle HQ, targeting 3 days a week in-office.
The salary range for this role is USD $110,000 - $140,000 annual base salary plus pre-IPO stock options and benefits. Individual compensation depends on factors such as role level, relevant experience, and skill set.
Benefits & Perks:
Pre-IPO stock options
Flexible time-off policy
HSA and PPO health insurance options
Dental and Vision insurance
401(k) plan
Choice of an ORCA card or parking subsidy
About Qumulo:
Built for the most demanding enterprise workloads, from AI and HPC simulations to Splunk Observability, genomics and PACS medical imaging, geospatial datasets, media editing and rendering, and video surveillance, Qumulo unlocks the full power of an organization’s information. Our platform unifies file and object storage across data centers, edge, and public clouds, enabling efficient, accelerated computing and extending the reach of data unbound by protocol or transport limitations.
With more than 1,100 customers and exabytes of data under management, Qumulo powers mission-critical workloads anywhere real-time access to massive file datasets is non-negotiable. Qumulo delivers radical simplicity, hardware freedom, exceptional customer support, and a true hybrid-cloud architecture.

At Qumulo, we are building an open and collaborative culture where people can do their best work with customers as our magnetic field. Firmware, embedded, and signal processing software running on custom hardware that flies the world’s largest fleet of spacecraft.
Cutting-edge networking algorithms capable of connecting thousands of satellites to millions of users in real time.
Infrastructure and tools enabling a highly reliable, software-defined global network.

JOB SUMMARY
Apptronik is seeking a Robotics Test Engineer to join the Software Integration & Test (RSIT) team. In this role, you will write the automated tests that verify Apollo's software at the integration layer, partner with senior engineers on defect investigations, and help grow the regression coverage that keeps each release safer than the last. You will work hands-on with our pytest-based test infrastructure, HIL benches, and the broader RSIT platform to turn software-level requirements into verifiable tests. This is a role designed for someone who wants to grow into deep expertise in robotics test engineering, with mentorship from senior teammates and meaningful ownership of test suites from day one.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES or KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES
Test Authoring: Write automated integration, contract, and ICD conformance tests in pytest against software-level requirements, with clear pass/fail signals that feed the release gate.
Defect Investigation: Partner with senior engineers on root-cause investigations for CI failures, escaped defects, and stochastic issues, building familiarity with debugging tools (sanitizers, log analysis, MCAP playback) over time.
Regression Coverage: Convert defects into permanent regression tests, ensuring every escape becomes a new automated check in the gate.
HIL Test Execution: Run and maintain test suites on hardware-in-the-loop benches, capture data, and report results into the team's dashboards and result reporting systems.
Test Suite Maintenance: Keep existing test suites healthy: triage flaky tests, update fixtures as the stack evolves, and improve readability and reliability of test code.
Requirements Engagement: Read software-level requirements and Systems Validation plans, ask clarifying questions, and surface ambiguity or untestable language to senior teammates and Systems Engineering.
Tooling Feedback: Serve as an active customer of the RSIT platform, surfacing friction in CI, dashboards, or release tooling so the Release & Integration team can improve developer experience.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with stack engineers, firmware engineers, and senior RSIT teammates to understand the systems being tested and produce verification that reflects how those systems actually behave.
SKILLS AND REQUIREMENTS
Programming: Working proficiency in Python, including ability to write clean, maintainable test code and small utility scripts. Comfort reading C++ to understand the systems under test.
Test Frameworks: Hands-on experience with pytest or an equivalent framework (unit test, Google Test, JUnit), including fixtures, parameterization, and test organization.
Linux Comfort: Day-to-day fluency on the Linux command line, including basic system, log inspection, file system navigation, and shell scripting.
Version Control: Solid Git fundamentals, including branching, pull requests, and code review participation.
Debugging Mindset: Demonstrated curiosity and persistence in tracking down bugs, including willingness to read code in unfamiliar parts of the stack to understand a failure.
Communication: Ability to write clear bug reports, test documentation, and pull request descriptions. Comfort asking questions and surfacing blockers early.
Learning Orientation: Eagerness to grow into deeper expertise in robotics, real-time systems, and verification engineering through mentorship, code review, and hands-on work.

Exposure to ROS or ROS2.
Experience with CI/CD systems (Bitbucket Pipelines, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or similar) as a user.
Familiarity with hardware-in-the-loop testing or other forms of hardware-integrated software verification.
Experience with observability tools (Grafana, Loki, Prometheus) as a consumer of dashboards and logs.
Background in robotics, autonomous systems, aerospace, or another hardware-integrated domain through coursework, internships, or prior roles.

Description
Marketing Measurement and Performance Science (MAPS) measures the incremental impact of Amazon's marketing investments on customer perception, action, and purchases — covering billions in annual fixed marketing (FM) spend across the full funnel. Our outputs provide spend insights and recommendations that power total investment decisions at the S-team level for OP planning, BU-level budget allocation, and in-year spend guidance.
As an SDE II, you'll design and build the systems that transform and harmonize data from 20+ external partners — each with their own schemas, grains, cadences, and nuances — into the measurement-grade inputs that power COSMOS, Amazon's FM causal measurement framework. The problems you will coverage go beyond standard ETL responsibilities — you'll build AI-native systems that reconcile providers with incompatible definitions, handle split metric ownership, manage retroactive revisions, and maintain the immutable snapshots and deterministic joins that causal inference demands.
Key job responsibilities
Design, develop, and maintain measurement-grade data systems at scale — ingesting, standardizing, and vending marketing data from 20+ external and internal sources that feed causal modeling and MLOps systems.
Own full lifecycle delivery of production software on complex, ambiguous problems — from design through launch and ongoing operations — with independence and minimal guidance.
Build automated validation pipelines and data quality frameworks that enforce contracts, detect anomalies across providers, and ensure measurement-grade integrity at every stage.
Define statistical methods for outlier detection, diagnose root causes systematically, and determine corrective actions to maintain data trust.
Partner across science, product, and engineering teams to scope solutions, navigate constraints, and ship the most efficient path from prototype to production.
Write clean, well-tested code (Python, Scala, or Java) and mentor junior engineers on system design, code quality, and operational best practices.
A day in the life
Day to day, you'll build and scale multi-layer automated validation pipelines, with clear data lineage so every model run is fully reproducible. Our vision is to scale our infrastructure across new business units and geographies reaching 90%+ coverage of Amazon's FM spend, and develop self-service catalog and observability tooling that lets scientists and partner teams explore our data without filing tickets. You'll also have a direct influence on schema governance — designing systems that enforce data standards at the point of contract, detect drift from providers, and keep our specifications current as partnerships expand.
You'll collaborate closely with causal scientists, economists, product managers, and agency data ops teams — translating measurement requirements into scalable technical solutions. This is a high-ownership role where your work directly determines whether Amazon's leadership can trust the numbers behind billion-dollar marketing investment decisions.
About The Team
Within MAPS, the Marketing Inputs & Data Automation (MIDA) team owns the measurement-grade data layer that sets the ceiling on what our causal models can measure, where they can operate, and how confident leadership should be in the outputs. We build and operate large-scale data infrastructure and data assets — ingesting, validating, harmonizing, and vending data from 20+ third-party providers (agencies, aggregators, publishers) across multiple Amazon business units and marketing channels, with global coverage. Our pipeline is purpose-built for the high bar of causal inference — not dashboards or reporting — requiring strict temporal integrity, historical stability, multi-layer validation, full lineage, and reproducibility at every stage.

3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
Experience programming with at least one software programming language
Experience programming with at least one modern language such as Java, C++, or C# including object-oriented design
Preferred Qualifications
3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

About Us
MintMCP helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. MintMCP scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.
We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.
We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.
Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.
The Job
You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.
We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.
About You
You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.
You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.
You care about product value and customer needs over technical purity.
You take infra seriously. You think about blast radius, trust boundaries, and what happens when your code is in the path of every customer's agents.
You can read unfamiliar code, reason from first principles, and explain your tradeoffs.

About ProEdge
ProEdge Dental Water Labs is a team of selfless builders. By putting our focus on the success of customers, we've created a healthy, quickly-growing, dynamic company. Our ~50 team has taken on a significant challenge: transform compliance in the dental practice—an often distinct pain for our customers—into a culture of shared purpose for the safety of patients and staff. By building trust and developing value-based solutions, we've created an emerging brand in dental.
Because of that, "good work" is the floor here. What we're building takes people who care more about the mission than the credit, who tell the truth before it's comfortable, and who would rather be stretched by real responsibility than protected from it.
Our Values
We build trust—by speaking candidly, doing what we say, and owning our mistakes.
We serve the team above ourselves—by choosing the mission over comfort, clarifying expectations, and engaging in feedback.
We delight our customers—by taking ownership of their experience, delivering quality they can count on, and treating every customer as valuable.
We create clarity—by making the goal plain, speaking up when we don't know, and closing the loop when clarity is at risk.
We improve—by driving our own growth, fixing the root, and making the better way repeatable.
The Software Engineer II Opportunity
Thousands of dental practices, from single offices to the largest dental groups in the country, use ProEdge's compliance platform to test their waterlines and sterilizers, see their results, and prove to inspectors that patients are safe. Our lab runs the tests. The platform is how the results reach the practice and how compliance is tracked, reminded, and reported. ProEdge is building its first in-house development team, and this role exists to make that platform one we own end to end: understood, covered by automated tests, deployed without downtime, and fast to change.
The team is two people: our Head of Technology and you. You will build with AI coding agents as the primary way code gets written, and your job is everything the agent cannot own: deciding what to build, specifying it precisely, reading every diff, proving it works, and answering for it in production. When you ship, the lab, our Customer Success team, and inside sales feel it the same week. A failed test that reaches a practice faster is a patient protected sooner.
Reports to:
Head of Technology, Kyle Crone
Success Outcomes
Every change to the platform ships through an automated, zero-downtime pipeline with one-click rollback that you and the Head of Technology can each run alone, within your first 90 days.
The compliance engine and permissions model are covered by automated tests below the browser, and the end-to-end suite is rebuilt in Playwright so that independent, trustworthy specs rise every month and the platform runs on one test framework by your six-month mark.
Inside sales and Customer Success work from data and reports built for them inside the platform, with a first cut in use within 120 days.
Two legacy modules are migrated to the target stack (TypeScript, typed SQL access, React) under tests with no customer-visible regression by month six, and the migration order is written down for the modules that follow.
Production is observable and safe: error tracking and alerting live, runbooks for the top failure modes, secrets in a managed store, and no critical or high dependency findings, within 90 days.
Core Responsibilities & Role Requirements
Core Responsibilities
Direct AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, or whatever is best next quarter) to build, then read every diff, write the tests, and own the result in production. Nobody will ask you to prove you can type it by hand; everybody will ask how you know it works.
Migrate the platform module by module from a homegrown JavaScript front end and an untyped Express API to TypeScript, typed SQL access, and React, using the strangler-fig pattern against live traffic. No big-bang rewrite, no cutover night.
Write Playwright end-to-end tests, API permission tests, and SQL tests around a compliance engine built from stored procedures and triggers, and keep the merge gate green as the team's source of truth.
Build and own the delivery platform on AWS (App Runner, Amplify Hosting, RDS, infrastructure as code with CDK): rolling deploys, rollback, monitoring, alerting, and managed secrets.
Ship the reporting, data views, and exports the inside sales and Customer Success teams need, and sit with the people who use them.
Own the platform's integrations: HubSpot for email, NetSuite for orders, the API our largest dental-group customers build on, and the data platform our BI team reports from.
Write it down: decision records, runbooks, and a living map of the system, plus the conventions and context files that let an agent or a new engineer be productive in the repo in minutes.
Share an on-call rotation with the Head of Technology once production is instrumented, and be steady when it misbehaves.
Role Requirements
Roughly three to six years shipping and operating web software people actually use.
Daily use of AI coding agents as your primary way of building, and the ability to show us your workflow live, including how you review, test, and correct what the agent produces.
Strong SQL. You can read and reason about stored procedures, triggers, and views (MySQL 8 or Postgres), and you have opinions about when logic belongs in the database.

If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.
The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.
About The Role
Health system call centers can't keep up with patient demand. 85% of patients who can't get through never call back. They go elsewhere, and appointments that should have been booked never are.
We're building AI Voice Agents that pick up every call and handle the full conversation: scheduling, rescheduling, cancellations, confirmations, FAQs, and intake. They work by integrating directly with the EHR and telephony stack in real time.
We're hiring a Software Engineer to build the systems these agents run on: the voice pipelines, EHR integrations, and services that take a call from "hello" to a booked appointment. It's a mid-level role on a small team that ships every day, with a lot of room to grow into harder problems.
This full-time position requires working 5 days a week in our Mountain View, CA office.
What You'll Do
Build backend services in Python that power real-time voice agents: call orchestration, conversation state, tool execution, and EHR write-back.
Contribute to low-latency pipelines connecting telephony, ASR, LLMs, and TTS into a single conversational loop.
Integrate with healthcare systems (like Epic, Cerner, athena, and others) for scheduling, eligibility, and intake.
Collaborate with senior engineers to design APIs, data models, and event-driven workflows.
Partner with AI, product, and operations to ship features patient access teams actually use.
Own the quality of what you ship: latency, reliability, observability, and release readiness.
What You Have
2–4 years of backend software experience, primarily in Python.
Experience shipping production services, APIs, and data models.
An intuition for how people interact with automated assistants through voice and text, where the rules are different than icons and buttons.
Comfort with async, event-driven, or real-time systems (or excitement to grow into them).
Strong fundamentals in testing, LLM evaluation, observability, and reliability.
A patient centered mindset. You design for the person on the other end of the line, not just the metrics.
Bias for action and an ownership mindset.

EDA R&D Engineer (C++, AI for Physical Design)
This is not a conventional Physical Design Engineer role. If your experience is primarily running P&R flows, even expertly and at advanced nodes, this probably isn't the one.
We're working with an early-stage semiconductor software company building AI-native optimization technology for backend chip implementation. The technology works alongside existing commercial EDA flows and tackles PPA optimization directly.

The strongest candidates demonstrate at least two of three areas:
EDA tool development
You've written production software inside EDA/CAD technology — placement, routing, timing, synthesis, DRC/physical verification, optimization algorithms or design-space exploration. We're looking for C/C++ development of the underlying technology, rather than simply scripts or flows around commercial tools.
Applied AI/ML
You've built or deployed models, agents, reinforcement learning or other ML/AI techniques against real engineering problems.
Exceptional physical design depth
You understand placement, routing, congestion, timing closure, PPA and/or physical verification deeply enough to understand why implementation tools behave the way they do — not simply how to operate them.
Two of the three is enough. Nobody is expected to have all three.
Backgrounds that fit
We're particularly interested in engineers from EDA vendor R&D teams, internal CAD/tool-development groups, semiconductor R&D organizations, university CAD research and technically ambitious startups.
Experience at an EDA vendor alone isn't enough. Application engineering, flow development and commercial-tool usage are different from developing the underlying EDA technology.
Startup experience is a plus, as is evidence that you've built something from scratch.
Seniority
We're deliberately flexible. Around 2–3 years of relevant industry experience is a useful starting point, but exceptional graduate researchers and engineers earlier in their careers are genuinely in scope. Experienced Senior/Staff engineers who remain deeply technical are equally relevant.
There is no specific PhD requirement. Technical profile matters more than years or academic pedigree.
